name: Jumping Jacks
description: Classic full-body cardio exercise. Jump feet apart while raising arms overhead, then return.
beginnerTips: Start slowly to master coordination. Land softly on balls of feet. Can be done low-impact by stepping instead of jumping.

name: High Knees
description: Running in place bringing knees up high. Excellent cardio exercise that also improves coordination.
beginnerTips: Run in place, bringing knees up toward chest. Pump arms naturally. Start with 20-30 seconds.

name: Butt Kicks
description: Running in place kicking heels toward glutes. Targets hamstrings while providing cardio benefits.
beginnerTips: Run in place, kick heels up toward glutes. Keep knees pointing down. Start with 20-30 seconds.

name: Burpees
description: Full-body explosive exercise combining squat, plank, push-up, and jump. Ultimate bodyweight cardio challenge.
beginnerTips: Start with step-back burpees (no jump). Master each component separately before combining. Land softly from jump.

name: Skater Jumps
description: Lateral jumping exercise mimicking ice skating motion. Develops power, balance, and cardiovascular fitness.
beginnerTips: Jump side to side, landing on one foot. Swing opposite arm across body. Start with small jumps.

name: Star Jumps
description: Explosive jumping exercise forming star shape. Jump up, spread arms and legs wide, then return.
beginnerTips: Jump up, spread arms and legs wide at peak. Land softly with feet together. Start with low jumps.

name: Tuck Jumps
description: Explosive jump bringing knees to chest. Develops power and cardiovascular fitness.
beginnerTips: Jump as high as possible, bringing knees toward chest. Land softly with knees slightly bent.

name: Inchworms
description: Full-body movement exercise. Stand, walk hands out to plank, then walk feet back to hands.
beginnerTips: Keep legs as straight as possible when walking hands out. Move slowly and controlled.

name: Shadow Boxing
description: Cardio exercise mimicking boxing movements. Throw punches in air, combining cardio with coordination.
beginnerTips: Throw jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts. Keep moving, don't stop between punches. 30-60 seconds rounds.

name: Jump Rope (No Rope)
description: Mimic jump rope motion without equipment. Jump lightly on balls of feet, rotating wrists as if holding rope.
beginnerTips: Jump lightly on balls of feet. Rotate wrists as if holding rope. Start with 20-30 seconds.

name: Fast Feet
description: High-intensity cardio exercise. Run in place as fast as possible, staying on balls of feet.
beginnerTips: Stay on balls of feet, move feet as fast as possible. Keep core engaged. Start with 10-15 second bursts.

name: Squat Jumps
description: Explosive squat variation with jump. Combines strength training with high-intensity cardio.
beginnerTips: Squat down, then explode up into jump. Land softly and immediately go into next rep.

name: Lunge Jumps
description: Explosive lunge variation with jump. Alternates legs while jumping, providing intense cardio workout.
beginnerTips: Start in lunge position, jump up and switch legs in air. Land in opposite lunge position.

name: Dancing in Place
description: Fun cardio exercise moving to music. Freestyle dance movements to get heart rate up.
beginnerTips: Move your body to music. Include arm movements, leg lifts, and hip movements. Have fun!

name: Jumping Lunges
description: High-intensity lunge variation with explosive jumps. Alternates legs while maintaining lunge position.
beginnerTips: Start in lunge, jump up and switch legs. Land softly in opposite lunge. Master regular lunges first.

name: Broad Jump
description: Explosive forward jump landing softly in an athletic stance. Develops power in legs and spikes heart rate for conditioning.
beginnerTips: Swing arms for momentum. Bend knees on landing to absorb impact.

name: Sprawl
description: Drop hips back, shoot legs out to plank, jump feet in, stand up. Burpee without the push-up—pure conditioning.
beginnerTips: Step feet back one at a time if jumping is too intense. Stand fully between reps.

name: Power Skips
description: Exaggerated skipping with explosive knee drive and arm swing. Develops single-leg power and high-intensity conditioning.
beginnerTips: Drive the opposite arm and leg together. Land softly on the ball of the foot.

name: Boxer Shuffle
description: Rapid weight shifts side to side on the balls of the feet with light punches optional. Low-impact cardio finisher.
beginnerTips: Stay on the balls of your feet. Keep movements small and rhythm steady.

name: Plank
description: Fundamental core exercise. Hold body in straight line supported by forearms and toes. Builds core strength and stability.
beginnerTips: Keep body straight from head to heels. Don't let hips sag or rise. Start with 20-30 seconds.

name: Side Plank
description: Unilateral core exercise performed on side. Targets obliques and improves lateral stability.
beginnerTips: Support body on one forearm and side of foot. Keep body straight. Start with 15-20 seconds per side.

name: Mountain Climbers
description: Dynamic core exercise alternating knees to chest. Combines strength with cardiovascular training.
beginnerTips: Start in plank position. Alternate bringing knees to chest. Keep hips level, don't bounce.

name: Bicycle Crunches
description: Rotational core exercise mimicking bicycle motion. Targets abs and obliques effectively.
beginnerTips: Lie on back, bring opposite elbow to knee. Extend other leg. Move slowly and controlled.

name: Russian Twists
description: Seated rotational exercise targeting obliques. Sit with knees bent, lean back slightly, rotate torso side to side.
beginnerTips: Keep core engaged and back straight. Rotate from torso, not just arms. Start without weight.

name: Flutter Kicks
description: Core exercise performed lying on back. Alternately kick legs up and down while keeping core engaged.
beginnerTips: Keep lower back pressed to floor. Move legs in small, controlled motions. Don't arch back.

name: Dead Bug
description: Core stability exercise performed on back. Extend opposite arm and leg while maintaining core engagement.
beginnerTips: Keep lower back pressed to floor. Move slowly and controlled. Alternate opposite arm and leg.

name: Bird Dog
description: Quadruped core stability exercise. Extend opposite arm and leg while maintaining balance.
beginnerTips: Start on hands and knees. Extend opposite arm and leg. Hold briefly, then switch sides.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Advanced isometric core exercise. Lie on back, lift shoulders and legs, hold position.
beginnerTips: Start with bent knees. Gradually straighten legs as you get stronger. Keep lower back pressed to floor.

name: V-Ups
description: Advanced core exercise forming V shape. Lie on back, lift torso and legs simultaneously to touch.
beginnerTips: Start with knees bent. Gradually work toward straight legs. Don't use momentum.

name: Toe Touches
description: Core exercise reaching for toes. Lie on back, lift legs and reach hands toward toes.
beginnerTips: Keep legs as straight as possible. Lift shoulders off ground. Reach up, not forward.

name: Reverse Crunches
description: Core exercise lifting hips. Lie on back, bring knees toward chest, lift hips off ground.
beginnerTips: Keep knees bent. Lift hips by contracting abs, not by swinging legs. Lower slowly.

name: Plank Jacks
description: Dynamic plank variation jumping feet apart and together. Combines core strength with cardio.
beginnerTips: Start in plank position. Jump feet apart and together while maintaining plank position.

name: Bear Crawl
description: Quadruped movement exercise. Crawl forward and backward on hands and feet, keeping knees off ground.
beginnerTips: Keep core engaged and back flat. Move opposite hand and foot together. Start with short distances.

name: Crab Walk
description: Reverse quadruped movement. Sit with hands behind you, lift hips, walk forward and backward.
beginnerTips: Keep hips lifted throughout. Move opposite hand and foot together. Start with short distances.

name: Windshield Wipers
description: Core exercise moving legs side to side. Lie on back, lift legs, rotate them side to side.
beginnerTips: Keep legs together and lower back pressed to floor. Move slowly and controlled.

name: L-Sit
description: Advanced isometric core exercise. Sit with legs extended, lift body off ground using core and arms.
beginnerTips: Start with bent knees or using chair for support. Gradually work toward full L-sit.

name: Plank to Downward Dog
description: Dynamic movement transitioning from plank to downward dog. Combines core strength with mobility.
beginnerTips: Start in plank, push hips up to downward dog, then return. Move slowly and controlled.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift
description: Advanced side plank variation. Hold side plank, lift top leg up and down.
beginnerTips: Master regular side plank first. Lift leg slowly, keeping body straight. Don't rotate hips.

name: Plank Up-Downs
description: Dynamic plank variation transitioning between high and low plank. Alternates between hands and forearms.
beginnerTips: Start in plank, push up to high plank one arm at a time, then lower back down. Keep core engaged.

name: Heel Taps
description: Lie on your back, crunch up slightly, and alternate tapping heels to the floor. Trains abs with light oblique engagement.
beginnerTips: Press lower back gently into the floor. Move slowly—do not rush the taps.

name: Knee Pull-In
description: Seated or on hands, draw knees toward chest and extend legs. Dynamic ab exercise scaling from beginner to advanced.
beginnerTips: Round lower back slightly as knees come in. Move slowly to avoid momentum.

name: Sit-up
description: Classic abdominal exercise. Curl torso up from the floor with feet anchored or bent, then lower with control.
beginnerTips: Exhale on the way up. If your neck strains, support your head lightly with your hands.

name: Standing Side Crunch
description: Stand tall and crunch sideways bringing elbow toward hip. Isolates obliques without lying on the floor.
beginnerTips: Keep hips level—avoid leaning the whole body. Contract the side you are crunching toward.

name: Cross-Body Mountain Climber
description: In high plank, drive knee toward opposite elbow. Adds rotation to mountain climbers for obliques and cardio.
beginnerTips: Keep shoulders over wrists. Quality beats speed—alternate sides with control.

name: Hollow Rock
description: Hold hollow body position and rock forward and back slightly. Advanced anti-extension core drill popular in gymnastics training.
beginnerTips: Master hollow hold first. Keep lower back pressed toward the floor.

name: Tuck Front Lever Hold
description: Hang from a bar, tuck knees, and depress shoulders to lift torso nearly horizontal. Advanced straight-arm back and core strength.
beginnerTips: Start with short tuck holds. Focus on pushing shoulders down away from ears.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: Fundamental lower body exercise. Stand with feet shoulder-width, lower down as if sitting in chair, then stand back up.
beginnerTips: Keep knees tracking over toes. Lower until thighs are parallel to floor or as low as comfortable.

name: Jump Squat
description: Explosive squat variation with jump at the top. Develops power and athleticism in lower body.
beginnerTips: Master regular squats first. Land softly with knees slightly bent to absorb impact.

name: Pistol Squat
description: Advanced single-leg squat. Requires exceptional strength, balance, and mobility. Ultimate leg strength test.
beginnerTips: Start with assisted pistol squats using a chair or holding onto something. Progress gradually.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Single-leg squat with rear foot elevated on chair. Excellent for building unilateral leg strength.
beginnerTips: Place rear foot on chair behind you. Lower down, keeping front knee over ankle. Start with shallow depth.

name: Forward Lunge
description: Unilateral leg exercise stepping forward. Targets quads, glutes, and improves balance.
beginnerTips: Step forward, lower back knee toward ground. Keep front knee over ankle. Push back to start.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: Lunge variation stepping backward. Easier on knees and emphasizes glutes more than forward lunge.
beginnerTips: Step backward, lower down until both knees form 90-degree angles. Push back to start position.

name: Walking Lunge
description: Dynamic lunge variation moving forward. Combines strength training with coordination.
beginnerTips: Start with stationary lunges. Alternate legs as you move forward, maintaining good form.

name: Jumping Lunge
description: Explosive lunge variation with jump between reps. Develops power and cardiovascular fitness.
beginnerTips: Master regular lunges first. Land softly and switch legs in the air. Start with low jumps.

name: Side Lunge
description: Lateral lunge variation stepping to the side. Targets inner thighs and improves hip mobility.
beginnerTips: Step to the side, lower down keeping other leg straight. Push back to center. Alternate sides.

name: Calf Raise
description: Isolated calf exercise. Stand on balls of feet, rise up onto toes, then lower down slowly.
beginnerTips: Rise up as high as possible, hold briefly, then lower slowly. Can be done on floor or elevated surface.

name: Single Leg Calf Raise
description: Unilateral calf exercise. Performed on one leg to increase difficulty and address imbalances.
beginnerTips: Master two-legged calf raises first. Hold onto something for balance if needed.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Hip extension exercise targeting glutes and hamstrings. Lie on back, lift hips up, squeeze glutes.
beginnerTips: Keep feet flat on floor, lift hips until body forms straight line. Squeeze glutes at the top.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
description: Advanced glute bridge variation performed on one leg. Significantly increases difficulty and glute activation.
beginnerTips: Master regular glute bridge first. Extend one leg straight, lift hips with one leg.

name: Donkey Kicks
description: Quadruped exercise targeting glutes. Start on hands and knees, kick one leg back and up.
beginnerTips: Keep core engaged and back straight. Lift leg without arching lower back. Squeeze glute at top.

name: Fire Hydrants
description: Quadruped exercise lifting leg to the side. Targets glutes and hip abductors.
beginnerTips: Start on hands and knees. Lift leg out to side, keeping knee bent. Don't rotate hips.

name: Clamshells
description: Side-lying exercise targeting hip abductors and glutes. Lie on side, lift top knee while keeping feet together.
beginnerTips: Keep feet together, lift only the knee. Don't roll backward. Move slowly and controlled.

name: Leg Raises
description: Core and hip flexor exercise. Lie on back, lift legs straight up, then lower down slowly.
beginnerTips: Keep lower back pressed to floor. Lower legs only as far as you can maintain back contact.

name: Single Leg Deadlift
description: Unilateral hip hinge exercise. Develops balance, hamstring strength, and glute activation.
beginnerTips: Start with small range of motion. Hinge at hips, extend opposite leg back. Keep back straight.

name: Skater Squats
description: Advanced single-leg squat variation. Requires exceptional balance and leg strength.
beginnerTips: Start with assisted version holding onto something. Lower down on one leg, extend other leg forward.

name: Step-up
description: Unilateral leg exercise using chair or step. Step up onto surface, then step back down.
beginnerTips: Use sturdy chair or step. Place entire foot on surface. Push through heel to step up.

name: Sumo Squat
description: Wide-stance squat variation. Targets inner thighs and glutes more than standard squat.
beginnerTips: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly out. Lower down, keeping knees tracking over toes.

name: Single Leg Squat
description: Advanced unilateral squat. Performed on one leg, requires exceptional strength and balance.
beginnerTips: Start with assisted version or pistol squat progression. Lower down on one leg, extend other leg forward for balance.

name: Cossack Squat
description: Lateral squat variation with one leg extended. Improves hip mobility and builds leg strength.
beginnerTips: Shift weight to one side, lower down while extending other leg. Keep extended leg straight.

name: Jump Squat to Tuck
description: Advanced jump squat variation bringing knees to chest in the air. Develops explosive power and core strength.
beginnerTips: Master regular jump squats first. Bring knees toward chest at peak of jump. Land softly.

name: Wall Sit Pulse
description: Dynamic wall sit variation. Hold wall sit position, then pulse up and down slightly.
beginnerTips: Start in wall sit position. Pulse up and down 2-3 inches. Keep back against wall throughout.

name: Squat Pulse
description: Hold the bottom of a squat and pulse up and down a few inches. Builds quad and glute endurance without equipment.
beginnerTips: Keep chest up and knees tracking over toes. Use a shallow range if needed.

name: Sissy Squat Hold
description: Lean back slightly while bending knees forward, keeping hips extended. Intense quad isolation using bodyweight only.
beginnerTips: Hold a wall or door frame lightly for balance. Use a small range until strength improves.

name: Sliding Hamstring Curl
description: Lie on your back, heels on a towel or socks on smooth floor, curl heels toward glutes. Hamstring curl without machines.
beginnerTips: Lift hips as you curl in. Control the slide back to start.

name: Nordic Curl Negative
description: Kneel with ankles anchored under a couch or partner, lower torso forward slowly, catch with hands. Advanced hamstring eccentric.
beginnerTips: Keep hips extended. Lower only as far as you can control—use hands to assist at the bottom.

name: Frog Pump
description: Lie on your back with soles together and knees open. Drive hips up by squeezing glutes for high-rep glute activation.
beginnerTips: Do not arch the lower back excessively. Pause briefly at the top of each rep.

name: Curtsy Lunge
description: Step one leg diagonally behind the other into a curtsy position and return. Emphasizes glutes and outer hip stability.
beginnerTips: Keep front knee aligned over the ankle. Touch the back knee toward the floor lightly.

name: Bodyweight Hip Thrust
description: Upper back on the floor, feet flat, drive hips to full extension. One of the most effective glute builders without weights.
beginnerTips: Tuck chin slightly and push through heels. Squeeze glutes hard at the top.

name: Standing Glute Kickback
description: Stand on one leg and drive the other leg straight back. Isolates glutes and improves hip extension strength.
beginnerTips: Squeeze glute at end range. Hold a wall for balance if needed.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: Sit with knees bent at 90 degrees and lift heels off the floor. Targets soleus and gastrocnemius without a step.
beginnerTips: Pause at the top. Place hands on knees for light resistance if desired.

name: Shrimp Squat
description: Single-leg squat reaching the back knee behind you while holding the rear foot. Advanced quad and balance challenge.
beginnerTips: Use a wall for balance. Progress from partial range to full depth over weeks.

name: Lateral Lunge Pulse
description: Step wide to one side, stay low, and pulse in the bottom position. Targets quads, glutes, and inner thighs.
beginnerTips: Keep the bent knee over the foot. Chest stays lifted throughout pulses.

name: Inverted Row
description: Bodyweight rowing exercise using a table or sturdy surface. Excellent for building back and bicep strength without equipment.
beginnerTips: Use a sturdy table or chair. Keep body straight, pull chest to surface. Adjust angle to change difficulty.

name: Superman
description: Prone exercise targeting lower back and glutes. Lie face down, lift arms and legs simultaneously, hold briefly.
beginnerTips: Lift only as high as comfortable. Focus on squeezing glutes and lower back muscles.

name: Reverse Snow Angels
description: Prone exercise where you move arms in snow angel motion. Strengthens posterior deltoids and upper back.
beginnerTips: Keep arms straight and lift them off the ground. Move slowly and controlled through full range of motion.

name: Y-T-W Raises
description: Prone exercise series forming Y, T, and W shapes with arms. Targets entire upper back and rear deltoids.
beginnerTips: Perform each letter shape separately. Keep core engaged and avoid arching lower back excessively.

name: Wall Angels
description: Standing exercise against wall mimicking snow angels. Improves posture and strengthens upper back muscles.
beginnerTips: Keep back, head, and arms in contact with wall. Move slowly and maintain contact throughout movement.

name: Prone Y Raise
description: Prone exercise lifting arms in Y position. Targets upper traps and rear deltoids.
beginnerTips: Lift arms at 45-degree angle. Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top.

name: Prone T Raise
description: Prone exercise lifting arms straight out to sides forming T shape. Strengthens rear deltoids and mid traps.
beginnerTips: Keep arms straight and lift them parallel to ground. Focus on squeezing shoulder blades.

name: Prone W Raise
description: Prone exercise with arms bent forming W shape. Targets rhomboids and rear deltoids.
beginnerTips: Bend elbows and lift arms, squeezing shoulder blades together. Keep core engaged.

name: Reverse Plank
description: Bodyweight exercise performed face-up. Strengthens posterior chain including back, glutes, and hamstrings.
beginnerTips: Start with bent knees and gradually straighten legs as you get stronger. Keep hips lifted.

name: Scapular Wall Slides
description: Posture exercise performed against wall. Strengthens upper back and improves shoulder mobility.
beginnerTips: Keep back, head, and arms against wall. Slide arms up and down while maintaining contact.

name: Isometric Pull Hold
description: Static hold exercise mimicking pull-up position. Builds grip strength and back endurance.
beginnerTips: Hang from a bar or sturdy surface. Hold chin over bar as long as possible. Use assistance if needed.

name: Reverse Plank Walk
description: Dynamic reverse plank variation. Walk hands backward while maintaining reverse plank position.
beginnerTips: Start with small steps. Keep hips elevated and body straight throughout movement.

name: Single Arm Row
description: Unilateral rowing exercise using bodyweight. Can be performed with towel or resistance band if available.
beginnerTips: Use a towel wrapped around a door handle or sturdy anchor. Pull with one arm, focusing on squeezing back muscles.

name: Towel Row
description: Rowing exercise using a towel for grip. Wrap towel around door handle or sturdy anchor and row.
beginnerTips: Ensure door or anchor is secure. Adjust distance to change difficulty. Closer = easier, farther = harder.

name: Doorway Row
description: Rowing exercise using doorway frame. Stand in doorway, pull body toward frame using back muscles.
beginnerTips: Use sturdy doorway. Place hands on frame, lean back, and pull body forward. Adjust angle for difficulty.

name: Australian Pull-up
description: Horizontal pulling exercise using table or bar. Body positioned horizontally, pull chest to surface.
beginnerTips: Use sturdy table or low bar. Keep body straight. Higher surface = easier, lower = harder.

name: Pull-up Negative
description: Eccentric phase of pull-up. Jump or step up to top position, then lower slowly. Builds strength for full pull-ups.
beginnerTips: Use a chair to reach top position. Lower as slowly as possible, aiming for 3-5 seconds descent.

name: Reverse Fly
description: Prone exercise mimicking reverse fly motion. Strengthens rear deltoids and upper back without weights.
beginnerTips: Lie face down, lift arms out to sides. Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top.

name: Wide Grip Inverted Row
description: Inverted row with hands placed wider than shoulder-width. Emphasizes outer back and rear deltoids.
beginnerTips: Use table or bar. Place hands wider than shoulders. Pull chest to surface while keeping body straight.

name: Close Grip Inverted Row
description: Inverted row with hands close together. Increases bicep emphasis and difficulty.
beginnerTips: Place hands close together, palms facing each other if possible. Pull with biceps and back muscles.

name: Prone Cobra
description: Back extension hold lying face down. Lift chest and arms slightly to strengthen the lower back and glutes with minimal spinal compression.
beginnerTips: Lift only as high as comfortable. Hold 2–3 seconds and lower with control.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
description: Hands behind head, hinge at hips with a flat back, then return upright. Strengthens hamstrings, glutes, and erectors.
beginnerTips: Push hips back as if closing a door with your glutes. Stop when torso is near parallel to the floor.

name: Chin-Up Negative
description: Underhand grip at the top of a chin-up, lower slowly for 3–5 seconds. Builds biceps and lat strength for full chin-ups.
beginnerTips: Use a sturdy bar. Jump or step to the top position and control the descent.

name: Dead Hang
description: Hang from a sturdy bar or ledge with arms straight. Builds grip, forearms, and decompresses the spine while preparing for pull-up strength.
beginnerTips: Pack shoulders down slightly. Start with 10–20 seconds and add time gradually.

name: Reverse Grip Hang Hold
description: Hang with underhand grip at the top of a chin-up position. Isometric hold for biceps and grip endurance.
beginnerTips: Use a box to reach the top position if needed. Keep shoulders engaged, not fully relaxed.

name: Fist Plank Hold
description: High plank performed on closed fists. Increases wrist and forearm demand while maintaining core tension.
beginnerTips: Align wrists under shoulders. Stop if you feel sharp wrist pain.

name: Scapular Push-up
description: From a high plank, protract and retract the shoulder blades without bending elbows. Trains serratus and mid-back control for healthier pressing.
beginnerTips: Keep arms straight throughout. Move only at the shoulder blades.

name: Renegade Row
description: From a high plank, row one hand to the hip while balancing on the other. Combines core stability with back and bicep pulling.
beginnerTips: Widen foot stance for stability. Prevent hips from rotating as you row.

name: Archer Inverted Row
description: Under a table, row toward one hand with the other arm extended. Unilateral back and bicep strength without a pull-up bar.
beginnerTips: Keep body rigid. Pull chest to the working hand each rep.

name: Push-up
description: Classic bodyweight exercise targeting chest, shoulders, and triceps. Start in plank position, lower body until chest nearly touches floor, then push back up.
beginnerTips: Start with knee push-ups if full push-ups are too difficult. Keep your core tight and body in a straight line.

name: Incline Push-up
description: Easier variation of push-up performed with hands elevated on a chair or wall. Reduces bodyweight load, perfect for beginners.
beginnerTips: Place hands on a sturdy chair or wall. The higher the surface, the easier the exercise.

name: Decline Push-up
description: Advanced push-up variation with feet elevated on a chair. Increases difficulty by shifting more weight to upper body.
beginnerTips: Start with a low elevation and gradually increase. Ensure the chair is stable and won't slide.

name: Diamond Push-up
description: Push-up variation with hands forming a diamond shape. Emphasizes triceps and inner chest muscles.
beginnerTips: Start with regular push-ups to build strength. Place thumbs and index fingers together to form diamond.

name: Wide Push-up
description: Push-up with hands placed wider than shoulder-width. Targets outer chest and shoulders more than standard push-up.
beginnerTips: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart. Keep elbows slightly flared out during movement.

name: Pike Push-up
description: Push-up performed in downward dog position. Excellent for building shoulder strength and preparing for handstand push-ups.
beginnerTips: Start with feet wider apart for better balance. Lower head toward floor between hands, then push back up.

name: Wall Push-up
description: Beginner-friendly push-up performed standing against a wall. Perfect for those building upper body strength.
beginnerTips: Stand facing wall, place hands on wall at shoulder height. Step back to increase difficulty.

name: Knee Push-up
description: Modified push-up performed on knees instead of toes. Reduces bodyweight load significantly.
beginnerTips: Keep your body straight from knees to head. Don't let your hips sag or rise too high.

name: Archer Push-up
description: Advanced unilateral push-up variation. Shifts weight to one arm while the other arm extends, building incredible strength.
beginnerTips: Master regular push-ups first. Start with a small shift and gradually increase the range.

name: Hindu Push-up
description: Dynamic push-up variation with flowing movement. Combines strength training with mobility work.
beginnerTips: Start in downward dog, lower into upward dog position, then return. Focus on smooth, controlled movement.

name: Spiderman Push-up
description: Push-up variation where you bring knee to elbow during the lowering phase. Adds core engagement and hip mobility.
beginnerTips: Start with regular push-ups. Add the knee movement once you're comfortable with the base exercise.

name: Shoulder Tap Push-up
description: Push-up variation where you tap opposite shoulder at the top of each rep. Challenges stability and core strength.
beginnerTips: Master regular push-ups first. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your body when tapping.

name: Tricep Dips
description: Upper body exercise using a chair. Targets triceps, shoulders, and chest. Sit on edge of chair, lower body, then push up.
beginnerTips: Keep feet closer to chair for easier variation. Ensure chair is stable and won't tip over.

name: Diamond Tricep Dips
description: Tricep dips with hands close together in diamond position. Increases tricep emphasis and difficulty.
beginnerTips: Master regular tricep dips first. Place hands close together with fingers pointing forward.

name: Wall Sit
description: Isometric leg exercise performed against a wall. Builds quadriceps and glute endurance.
beginnerTips: Slide down wall until thighs are parallel to floor. Hold position with back flat against wall.

name: Pseudo Planche Push-up
description: Advanced push-up with hands positioned further back toward waist. Extremely challenging variation that builds incredible strength.
beginnerTips: Start with hands slightly behind shoulders and gradually move them back as you get stronger.

name: Clapping Push-up
description: Explosive push-up variation where you clap hands together at the top. Develops power and upper body explosiveness.
beginnerTips: Master regular push-ups first. Start with small claps and gradually increase height. Land softly.

name: One-Arm Push-up
description: Ultimate push-up challenge performed with one arm. Requires exceptional strength, stability, and core control.
beginnerTips: Progress from archer push-ups. Start with feet wide apart and gradually bring them closer together.

name: Handstand Push-up
description: Advanced exercise performed in handstand position. Ultimate test of shoulder strength and stability.
beginnerTips: Master handstand hold first. Practice against a wall before attempting freestanding. Use pike push-ups to build strength.

name: Dive Bomber Push-up
description: Dynamic push-up variation combining downward dog, low push-up, and upward dog positions in one fluid motion.
beginnerTips: Start slowly to master the movement pattern. Focus on smooth transitions between positions.

name: Staggered Push-up
description: Push-up with one hand slightly forward and one back. Builds unilateral pressing strength and core stability while training chest and arms.
beginnerTips: Keep hips square to the floor. Alternate which hand is forward each set.

name: Tempo Push-up
description: Push-up with a slow 3-second lowering phase and explosive press up. Increases time under tension for chest and triceps.
beginnerTips: Count three seconds down, one second up. Maintain a rigid plank throughout.

name: Close-Hand Push-up
description: Push-up with hands shoulder-width or slightly narrower. Shifts emphasis toward triceps while still loading the chest.
beginnerTips: Keep elbows closer to the body than a standard push-up. Do not let hips sag.

name: Arm Circles
description: Shoulder mobility and endurance drill. Extend arms to the sides and draw controlled circles to warm up and strengthen the deltoids.
beginnerTips: Start with small circles and gradually enlarge them. Reverse direction halfway through the set.

name: Prone I Raise
description: Lie face down and lift straight arms overhead forming an I shape. Targets rear delts and upper back for posture and shoulder health.
beginnerTips: Keep thumbs pointing up. Squeeze shoulder blades at the top without shrugging.

name: Body Saw
description: From forearm plank, rock body forward and back using shoulders. Challenges core anti-extension and triceps endurance.
beginnerTips: Move in a small range at first. Keep glutes engaged to protect the lower back.

name: Typewriter Push-up
description: At the bottom of a push-up, shift body weight side to side before pressing up. Extreme chest and tricep tension with core demand.
beginnerTips: Stay low—move horizontally at the bottom only. Master archer push-ups first.

name: Meditation & Deep Breathing
description: Focused mindfulness session. Sit or lie still, close your eyes, and practise box breathing: inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 4s, hold 4s. Reduces cortisol and accelerates recovery.
beginnerTips: Start with 5-minute sessions. A wandering mind is normal — gently redirect to the breath without judgement.

name: Easy Jog / Brisk Walk
description: Low-intensity steady-state cardio. Keep pace conversational — you should complete full sentences without gasping. Promotes blood flow and active recovery without adding training stress.
beginnerTips: If your heart rate exceeds 130 bpm, slow to a walk. The goal is circulation, not intensity.

name: Full Body Mobility Flow
description: Dynamic and static stretching targeting major muscle groups in sequence. Improves range of motion, reduces soreness, and primes the body for the next training day.
beginnerTips: Move at breath pace. Never bounce into a stretch. Work from ankles upward: ankles to hips to thoracic spine to shoulders to neck.
